What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0175-0005 at 10:30 on 2022-11-17 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.2% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

Asset: WELL-0175 (NE-08 Well 175, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 01 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Dec 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 932 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0175-0104 on 2024-10-31 Report written: 12 Dec 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0175-0104 showed the wellhead at 27.8 °C with the air at 22.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0175-020

Asset: WELL-0175 (NE-08 Well 175, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 01 Feb 2025 08:00 · Finished: 05 Feb 2025 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 97 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0175-0117 on 2025-01-30 Report written: 06 Feb 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0175-0117 showed the wellhead at 9.4 °C with the air at 8.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service
